summary.text: Big Thief's audience gravitates toward intimate, emotionally open singer-songwriting and indie folk across the Northeast, with strong fan hotspots in Boston, Burlington, Portland ME, Northampton, and Albany. This five-city tour targets mid-sized rooms (300–900 capacity) where the artist's confessional, vulnerability-centered music aligns with venues specializing in folk, indie, and alternative rock.

why.text: 89 room affinity in Boston, near a Qloo fan hotspot. Alston Village cluster favors straightforward, melodic folk and indie. Suggested opener Lucy Dacus shares Big Thief's introspective, drum-driven songwriting.

pitch.text: Big Thief brings introspective, vulnerability-centered indie folk to Boston fans with strong affinities for sensitive, confessional songwriting. Audiences in Allston Village engage deeply with melodic folk and indie with simple chord progressions—a core strength of Big Thief's catalogue. We're looking at rooms of 300–900 (our own target). Lucy Dacus as a suggested opener brings shared melodic and drum-forward sensibilities. We'd love to book a run here.

The Old North End cluster shows particular affinity for straightforward songwriting with simple chord progressions—core to Big Thief's appeal. We'd approach Julia Jacklin to open, sharing those melodic, folk-forward sensibilities. Strong fit for your audience.

This five-city tour targets mid-sized rooms (300–900 capacity) where the artist's confessional, vulnerability-centered music aligns with venues specializing in folk, indie, and alternative rock.

theme.text: "Confessions & Quiet Storms": Frame the show around Big Thief's gift for turning internal grief and vulnerability into melodic, straightforward narratives. Emphasize the human experience and sensitivity at the heart of the music.
"Folk Unfiltered": Highlight how Big Thief strips songwriting to simple chord progressions and honest storytelling, letting melody and introspection carry the emotional weight.
"Intimacy in the Room": Center on the close, unguarded connection between artist and audience in mid-sized venues—where every word lands and the confessional quality of the music becomes immersive.

merch.text: Outdoor/hiking apparel capsule (hats, socks, technical layers) in collaboration with brands fans favour—Patagonia, Fjällräven, or Pendleton. Aligns with the indie folk and environmental values of the audience.
Limited-run lyric sheets or handwritten confessional booklets, printed on recycled or sustainable paper. Speaks to fan values around introspection and human connection.
Vinyl reissues or tour-exclusive editions on eco-conscious labels. Appeals to audiences who engage with folk and indie as collectors of deliberate, high-fidelity recorded music.

risks.text: Venues and openers are suggestions based on Qloo data; final booking and availability depend on direct venue and artist negotiation. Dates, competing shows, and routing logistics require coordination.

Data reflects aggregate national fan demographics (ages 24 and younger +0.27, 30–34 +0.36, female +0.26) but cannot predict local audience composition at each stop. Demographic variation by city is not captured here.
